### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/inner-refusal.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via innerRefusal (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand), userMessage (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand), RESUME_FAILED (literal, a string literal in parentStrandReport; a string literal in recall; a string literal in resumeBatchOfRecalledItem; a string literal in resumeRecordedOutcome))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class), bubbleToParent (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), RESUME_FAILED (literal, a string literal in parentStrandReport; a string literal in recall; a string literal in resumeBatchOfRecalledItem; a string literal in resumeRecordedOutcome))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via describeEffectiveAccess (sdk, the bare tail of client method security.describeEffectiveAccess, bound to GET /api/v1/security/users/:id/effective-access))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand))_
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand))_

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface ResumeFailureReport; a field of interface SubflowParentStrand))_

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via RESUME_FAILED (literal, a string literal in parentStrandReport; a string literal in recall; a string literal in resumeBatchOfRecalledItem; a string literal in resumeRecordedOutcome))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/inner-refusal.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f848e3739f36fdfadc58cb4ce07defda6e624cba` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b81c3ddef97ab4d7b101a16f8bbb5f525435967c` — the merge of head `8c0b7ce7a05a10278f47c1c99baed3c674882425` into base `f848e3739f36fdfadc58cb4ce07defda6e624cba`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b81c3ddef97ab4d7b101a16f8bbb5f525435967c && git checkout b81c3ddef97ab4d7b101a16f8bbb5f525435967c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f848e3739f36fdfadc58cb4ce07defda6e624cba 8c0b7ce7a05a10278f47c1c99baed3c674882425 && git checkout -B drift-repro f848e3739f36fdfadc58cb4ce07defda6e624cba && git merge --no-ff 8c0b7ce7a05a10278f47c1c99baed3c674882425

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f848e3739f36fdfadc58cb4ce07defda6e624cba
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f848e3739f36fdfadc58cb4ce07defda6e624cba` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9b417c941ddf021399952547b23edc40d2c5fb86`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/inner-refusal.ts
Security-touching: no

Inputs read: card #34638 (body and all six comments), PR #34999 (body, file list, its three comments, and the net diff from merge base `e9f65a3b` to this head), and the check-runs on this head. The seat's L1 ACCEPT comment on the PR was fetched with the others and is not used as evidence. Read to judge, never reviewed: the cited code at this head (`run-resume.ts`, `runtime-identity.ts` and `dag-traversal.ts` in `service-automation`; `packages/types/src/stranded-decision.ts`; `packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts`; `api/automation-api.zod.ts` and `contracts/automation-service.ts` in spec; the hook refusal catalogue in `packages/runtime`), the two rulings the contract cites (the #16472 ruling, comment 5567695080; ruling B′ on #24914, comment 6303788292) and the record on PR #34619 that filed this card (6938300180). The two new test files, the type pin and the pin ledger are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; they were read only to see what the head pins.

Check-runs on this head: 69, all completed. 58 concluded `success` and 11 `skipped`; none failed and none is pending. The successes include Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Test Core and its ten shards, Build Core, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check UI, Test UI and its sixteen shards, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI and Dogfood Regression Gate. Lint UI concluded `skipped`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ResumeFailureReport` (`@objectstack/spec/contracts`) gains `innerRefusal?: FlowInnerRefusal` and `userMessage?: string`. Right: both are optional, `innerRefusal` reuses the type declared once in `api/automation-api.zod.ts`, and `code`, `runId`, `status` and `repairable` keep their types and meanings. The report minus what it adds is still `ResumeFailureDetails`.
- `ApprovalRecallResult.resumeFailure` and `ApprovalDecisionResult.resumeFailure` widen through that type alone. Right: both stay optional under the same absence rule.
- No Zod schema moves (`ResumeFailureDetailsSchema`, `FlowFailureDetailsSchema` and `FlowInnerRefusalSchema` are untouched) and no export is added or removed. Right: no generated artifact is owed, and the spec artifact gates in TypeScript Type Check are green.
- Wire: the 200 answers of `POST …/approvals/requests/:id/recall` and of the decision doors gain two optional keys inside `resumeFailure`, present only when the engine reported them. Right: the REST door relays the service result verbatim (`res.json(out)`), and the status code, `resumed`, `resumeError` and the four existing report members answer what they answered before. A consumer that asserted the exact four-key report sees up to six on a refused strand, which the member's "Optional and ADDITIVE" already allowed.
- `SubflowParentStrand`, the return value of `AutomationEngine.takeSubflowParentStrand` (`@objectstack/service-automation`), gains the same two optional members. Right: additive on a return value.
- `ApprovalResumeSurface.takeSubflowParentStrand` (`@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, the surface a host implements) now returns its three members plus the optional pair. Right: a host that returns the three-member shape still satisfies it, and what the service reads from the engine widens by two optional members.
- No error code is minted. Right: the report's `code` is still this package's one registered literal, `RESUME_FAILED`, and `innerRefusal.code` is relayed from the engine.
- The thrown `RESUME_FAILED` envelope and `StrandedDecisionDetails` are untouched. Right: the decision door's own strand answers exactly what it answered.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` is right. `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right kind, since nothing a metadata author can write changes, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task step 3). The three packages the diff moves are the three named; `@objectstack/rest` only relays and `@objectstack/types` is untouched. Check Changeset concluded `success`.
- `Clause-②: yes` is right, and it is line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body: a published type grows by two optional members and nothing accepted before is refused.
- Nothing is breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition and no migration is owed; the changeset's "No migration" sentence is right.
- Changeset prose against the diff: accurate, except the parenthesis "(the declared sentence in the caller's locale)". That is S1 below. The changeset ships as CHANGELOG text, so it is corrected in the same edit as the docblock.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question, where the pair is declared: on `ResumeFailureReport` only, as pushed.
  - On the resume door both members already have a declared home under ruling B′: `details.innerRefusal` in `FlowFailureDetailsSchema`, and `userMessage` at the envelope's top level. A client parses that one `details` object with both schemas, so `innerRefusal` on `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema` would declare one key of one object twice.
  - `userMessage` on `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema` would declare a `details` key that `FlowFailureDetailsSchema` says is not a details key, past the ceiling ruling B′ set, and one the resume door never fills.
  - The #16472 ruling asks for one structure declared once and reused by its three carriers. That is the three shared members, and they stay inherited. The pair is added where a carrier has no envelope, which is the reason `code` sits on the report and not on the schema.
  - One consequence is left untold in the docblock: N1.
- Triage on the card (6938361547) said no maintainer card is needed unless this review finds otherwise. It does not: the #16472 ruling fixes what a report must carry and forbids a new code, and caps no further member; ruling B′'s semantics for the pair are kept (④).
- The PR was opened by the seat on the maintainer's order and its body is the seat's; the PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, and the diff is the dev's pushed branch. No effect on the contract. The body's Verification paragraph (the dev's local counts and ablations) is not relied on here; the check-runs above are the verdict.
- Out of the claim's listed surface, `inner-refusal.ts`: accepted. The hunk is a docblock, and it is the sentence the `engine.ts` hunk would otherwise leave false ("no caller reads their result").
- Out of the claim's listed surface, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: the lane seat's. It adds two rows for the new test file's engine double and removes none.
- The claim listed `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema` and the diff does not touch it. That agrees with the answer above.
- `Security-touching: no`, and why. No hunk adds, removes or changes a permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication check, and none teaches one. On disclosure: the refusal's diagnostic text already reaches the same caller on the same answer in `resumeError` (the recall door copies the resume failure text, and the parent-strand prose embeds the strand's `error`), so `innerRefusal.message` is a substring of what that caller reads today. `userMessage` is new on these answers. It is the text its producer marked for end users, no access decision reads it, and the decision doors' 500 has carried it since #34579. On a parent strand the refused write ran under the parent run's own principal and the reader is the door's caller. I read that as a relay of text already meant for end users, not as security behaviour, so the line reads `no`.
- `Reviewed-by`: this record was rendered by an isolated reviewer sub-agent. Its environment names no session of its own (its remote session is the seat's), so the line carries the seat's session, as the brief directs. The diff was produced by the dev's branch; the seat wrote the PR body only.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Outside the diff, not a finding on this head: `resumeRecordedOutcome` also serves the auto-reject, send-back and resubmit doors, and those keep `resumeError` and drop `resumeFailure` (their result types declare none). A parent strand behind an auto-reject therefore reaches its caller as prose only, the refusal included. That is older than this PR, and the card scoped the recall door and the parent strand through `decide` and `recall`. The seat may file it.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` (the `hits` file), against the rulings it implements and its first consumer:

- The #16472 ruling holds. The report still tells the registered code, the stranded run's id and `repairable`, the status code does not move, and the pair is optional, additive and "never part of the failure class".
- Ruling B′ holds for `innerRefusal`: it is the engine's own member under the type declared once, nested beside the report's `code` and never replacing it, present only when a refusal was met and never synthesised from prose.
- `userMessage` rides inside `resumeFailure`, not at the top level of the 200 answer. Right: the top-level `userMessage` is the error envelope's channel, and this answer is a success. The rewritten prohibition on `ApprovalDecisionResult.resumed` says so and stays true, because the decision door's own strand still rides the error.
- That rewrite reverses no ruling. The prohibition it rewrites was already there before PR #34619 (that PR's record calls it existing), and what it guarded still holds: the decision door's own strand is never told on the success answer. Whether `resumeFailure` should carry the pair was left to a follow-up card by that record (its N2), and this card is that follow-up.
- The channel map in the interface docblock is accurate: the resume door carries `innerRefusal` in `error.details` and `userMessage` at the envelope's top level, and the decision doors' thrown `RESUME_FAILED` carries both on its body.
- First consumer: the producer in `plugin-approvals` and its tests. No reader of `resumeFailure` exists in `ui/` or `packages/client` at this head, so the docblock is all a future reader has. That is why S1 matters.

S1 (should-fix) — `ResumeFailureReport.userMessage` says the hook's sentence is "in the caller's locale"; on this channel the tree serves the run's locale.
- Every strand this report tells is a resumed leg: the recall door's own resume, or the bubble that resumes a parent.
- `AutomationContext.locale`, in the same package, states the rule: a resumed leg renders in the starter's locale "whoever resumes it", and a run no person started (a record-change, schedule or webhook trigger) carries none.
- The code follows that rule. `resolveRunDataContext` hands the run's `locale` to the write ("worded for the person who started the run"), `deciderSegmentContext` moves `userId` and the grants to the decider and leaves `locale`, and `serviceResume` hands the engine no locale.
- So an approver whose decision strands a subflow parent reads the language of whoever started the run (usually the submitter), and a record-change run answers the hook's declared message as authored.
- Everywhere else in this docblock "caller" is the reader of the report, so the sentence promises the reader's language. The changeset repeats it in a parenthesis, and the PR body's summary line does too.
- Nothing in the head pins it: the new approvals test says in its header that the locale is "the runtime's choice" and pins the carrier only.
- Fix, wording only, in the member docblock and the changeset: the run's locale, which is the language of whoever started the run, and the authored message when no person started it.
- The same sentence has stood on `StrandedDecisionDetails.userMessage` in `@objectstack/types` since PR #34619. That file is outside this diff, so correcting it or filing it is the seat's. Whether a decision should be re-worded for the decider is a design question for its own card.

Implementing files, sentence by sentence:

- `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts`: agrees. The strand is recorded only on the `'stranded'` exit, and `carriedRefusalOfResult(parentRes)` copies what that exit put on the parent's own result (`...readCarriedRefusal(err)` in `run-resume.ts`). A fault spreads nothing, so "absent, never synthesised from `error`'s text" holds.
- `packages/services/service-automation/src/inner-refusal.ts`: agrees. The added exception is true: a parent on the `'stranded'` exit does carry the members on its result, and the strand is now the one reader of them.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`: agrees on what is filled, and where. There are five construction sites of `resumeFailure` and all five carry the pair: the three parent-strand sites through `parentStrandReport`, and the recall door's own strand and the batch resume's own strand through `resumeRefusalOf(err)`. The exits that report nothing still report nothing. It does not agree on how the pair is read: S2.

S2 (should-fix) — the success channel skips the two reads the thrown channel applies, so the two approvals channels can answer one engine result differently.
- On the thrown path `strandedDecisionDetails` drops an `innerRefusal` whose `code` is outside the closed `ErrorCode` set or whose `message` is not a string, and reads `userMessage` through `declaredUserMessage`, so a blank or non-string value is not a marking.
- On this path `serviceResume` keeps both members whenever they are not `undefined`, the recall arm and the batch arm spread them last into the report, and `parentStrandReport` copies the strand's members the same way.
- The engine's own data nodes never produce a malformed member. But the engine brands whatever a node executor returns (`attachCarriedRefusal(…, result)` in `dag-traversal.ts`; `pickCarried` passes any string and any defined `innerRefusal`), and node types are open to plugins.
- A plugin node that returns a blank `userMessage` on the step after a recall puts a blank `userMessage` on the 200 answer, where the contract says "presence IS the marking" with the "same semantics as on every other channel". The same result through `decide` carries none. An unregistered `innerRefusal.code` likewise reaches the wire under a member typed with the closed set.
- The diff also leaves a standing sentence in `serviceResume` false: "the recogniser in `@objectstack/types` validates it before anything reaches the wire". That was true while the thrown envelope was the only reader; the recall and batch reports now read the same value with no recogniser.
- Fix: apply the same two reads once where the pair is built for this channel (`serviceResume` and `parentStrandReport`), and correct that comment.

Break attempts that did not break it:
- A fault-stranded run or parent carries neither member: the fault spreads nothing on the recall door's own strand, on the batch resume's own strand, or on any parent strand.
- A parent strand names the parent's run id and the parent's refusal, never the child's.
- A strand is deleted on read, so no refusal from an earlier resume can ride a later report.
- The exits with no report (a lost run, the tolerated duplicate, a failure with no engine status) gain nothing.
- With the engine's own producers the spread cannot overwrite `code`, `runId`, `status` or `repairable`, because `serviceResume` builds the carried object with the two keys only.
- No lookup failure can reach the batch report: `batchRunId` is set only just before the resume.

Nits:

- N1 (nit) — the ⛔ paragraph on `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema` still counts `code` as the one member a parse strips. Since this diff the parse strips the refusal pair too (the head's own pin measures it), and "Which is exactly why" now follows the refusal sentence, not the `code` one.
